subject: Encryption artifacts request: TLS cipher list + keystore operator separation
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@bluecrest.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@bluecrest.com
Date: 2028-07-22T15:10:00Z
Subject: Request: TLS cipher inventory + operator separation evidence for SOC2

Hi Karthik,

As part of our SOC 2 readiness review we need a short evidence bundle covering network encryption and keystore/operator controls for the Redwood tenant we'll onboard. Can you provide the following by end of week?

- Active TLS cipher suites on your public API endpoints (including minimum TLS version and any TLS termination points).
- Keystore operator separation: list of operator roles with access windows and a sampling of operator shift logs (redacted is fine).
- HSM attestation or vendor statement for in-use HSMs (if keys are wrapped or kept outside cloud KMS).
- A 30-day sample of key rotation metadata (timestamps, operator id or automation id, key IDs) for customer-encrypted keys.

I've attached a short questionnaire (bluecrest-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx) with fields we will import into our compliance tracker. If you can point me to an SFTP or shared location for the artifacts that works too.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Park
Security Assurance Manager | Bluecrest Finance
alice.park@bluecrest.com
[attachment: bluecrest-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: TLS cipher inventory + operator separation evidence for SOC2

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High level: Redwood terminates TLS at our edge proxies (TLS 1.2+ enforced; we are rolling to TLS 1.3 preferred), and key material for customer-managed keys may be held in customer BYOK HSMs or in our dedicated KMS depending on the deployment.

Action plan (quick):
- I'll surface the active cipher suite inventory and TLS termination topology (edge, internal service-to-service) by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa will prepare the keystore operator manifest and a 30-day rotation sample; we'll redact PII in operator logs.
- We can produce an HSM vendor attestation or the KMS vendor statement depending on your tenant (I'll flag which applies in the bundle).

I'll put the artifacts onto a scoped SFTP and send transfer instructions. Looping in Marissa for artifacts and transfer.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: TLS cipher inventory + operator separation evidence for SOC2

Hi Alice — uploading the initial artifact set now. Summary of included items: 

1) redwood-keystore-operator-manifest.csv — operator roles and last access windows (sensitive fields redacted).
2) redwood-rotation-sample-2028Q2.csv — 30-day rotation events for customer tenant keys (key_id, rotation_timestamp_utc, actor_type: automation|operator, operator_id-redacted).
3) tls-inventory.txt — active cipher suites at the edge and internal mTLS policies.
4) hsm-statement.pdf — vendor-supplied statement for our hosted HSM fleet where applicable (if your tenant selected BYOK we will provide the customer HSM attestation instead).
5) sftp-transfer-instructions.txt — credentials and path (one-time, expires in 7 days).

A couple of implementation notes to save time during review:
- TLS: Edge proxy terminates customer-facing TLS (TLS 1.2 minimum, we advertise TLS 1.3). Internal service-to-service connections use mTLS with mutual certs and short-lived certs rotated via our CA at a 24-hour cadence for ephemeral nodes. Cipher preference is AEAD suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384), and we do not support CBC ciphers on public endpoints.
- Keystore ops: Operator separation follows our runbook — human operator actions require two-person approval for high-privilege operations; routine rotations are automated via scheduled jobs that are auditable in our rotation ledger.
- Redactions: operator_id values are pseudonymized (OP-###) in the sample to protect staff PII; full operator audit trails can be produced under an MOU if needed.

Transfer/links: I'm placing the files on our SFTP this afternoon. Link: sftp://sftp.redwood-secure.com/incoming/bluecrest_2028/ (see attachment with connection details). If Bluecrest prefers a signed DocuSign access authorization for the full operator audit we can follow that route — I've included a placeholder envelope if you want it: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123xyz

Attachments included: redwood-keystore-operator-manifest.csv, redwood-rotation-sample-2028Q2.csv, tls-inventory.txt, hsm-statement.pdf, sftp-transfer-instructions.txt

From: Alice Park <alice.park@bluecrest.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: TLS cipher inventory + operator separation evidence for SOC2

Marissa — thanks for the quick turn. I downloaded the CSVs and the tls-inventory. A couple quick clarifications before we import to our tracker: 

1) In the rotation sample the actor_type column includes both "automation" and "operator" — when operator is present, will you share the approval artifact ID or a trace id we can map to an approval event? The approval artifact id is fine if operator identity remains pseudonymized.
2) For the HSM statement: is the PDF a vendor-signed attestation, or an internal summary prepared by Redwood? If vendor-signed, can you provide the vendor contact for verification?

If you can reply to those two points we'll proceed with our intake. Appreciate the MOU note — we'll coordinate with procurement if we need full operator logs.

Best,
Alice
Security Assurance Manager | Bluecrest Finance
alice.park@bluecrest.com
